text: I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me your name and what has been happening with your behavior lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: The mental status exam was reported as normal, but his delusions and functional decline over six weeks strongly suggest a primary psychotic disorder like schizophrenia. To rule out organic causes such as a brain tumor or autoimmune encephalitis, I need to see structural and functional brain data, so REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical or psychiatric history reported. Social history: Previously employed. No history of substance abuse reported. Married.

speaker: Doctor

speaker: Doctor
text: With a normal MRI and negative drug screen, the persistent delusions and functional decline over six weeks strongly point to a primary psychotic disorder. I need to confirm the duration of symptoms and rule out mood components to distinguish between schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder. Do you have any history of manic episodes, or have you experienced significant depressed mood independent of your delusions?

speaker: Patient
text: No significant findings. Denies any drug use, recent travel, or physical health issues.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the six-week duration of delusions and functional decline with normal medical workup, I am ruling out brief psychotic disorder and substance-induced psychosis. I have enough information to proceed with a primary psychotic disorder diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophreniform Disorder
